final_answer:
Merge sort works by recursively dividing the input into smaller subarrays until each subarray contains a single element, which is inherently sorted. Then, it merges these subarrays back together in a sorted manner. The merging process involves comparing the front elements of each subarray and appending the smaller one to the result, repeating until all elements are combined into one sorted array. This divide-and-conquer approach ensures a time complexity of O(n log n) in all cases.

Merge sort is preferred over quicksort for linked lists because linked lists do not support efficient random access, which quicksort relies on for selecting pivot elements. In contrast, merge sort can split and merge linked lists without requiring random access, making it more suitable for this data structure. Additionally, merge sort’s stable nature and consistent performance make it a better choice for linked lists, where operations like swapping elements are more costly than in arrays. Safe.
